Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and G2111; not well set, i.e. inconvenient:--not commodious.
BiblicalUsage: Paul's ship is caught in a storm and the sailors fear the place is not commodious to winter in, so they sail on toward Crete. The word means an inconvenient harbour, a place not fit to wait out the winter.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for an unfit harbour carries no teaching of its own; its interest is the voyage, that a bad wintering place pushed Paul's ship on toward the storm.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
